newsitem.title: GERMANY: German bank shares surge in early IBIS trade.
newsitem.headline: German bank shares surge in early IBIS trade.

text.p: Shares in German banking stocks surged in early electronic trade on Monday after Bayerische Hypo-Bank and Bayerische Vereinsbank announced they were planning to merge.
Vereinsbank opened IBIS trade at 92 marks, up 12.2 percent from Friday's level, while Hypo-Bank opened at 73 marks, a rise of 25 percent on Friday's close of 58 marks.

Shares in insurer Allianz AG were down three marks at 436 marks in early IBIS trade. Vereinsbank said that it was going to offer Allianz shares to Hypo-Bank shareholders, where they receive one Allianz share for six Hypobank shares.
The opening price for the Hypo-Bank share is close to the offer price, which equates to 75 marks per Hypo-Bank share.
The merger news lifted the IBIS DAX index nearly 1.7 percent in early trade to 4,205 points before settling back slightly to 4,198.50 points.
Dresdner Bank was up 5.04 marks at 80.30 marks, Commerzbank was up 3.66 marks at 57.16 marks, while Deutsche Bank rose 3.35 marks to 110.25 marks.
